claims.statement: Root cause is NOT allocation rule v18 logic defect; it is a downstream issue (carrier feed lag, inventory count drift, or dock capacity) on the east node affecting both split-reservation and standard allocations
claims.corroboration: Reverting v18 to v17 did not resolve held orders; new east-node allocations remain stuck under v17 rule. This conclusively disproves v18-logic defect and indicates a persistent downstream constraint affecting all east-node allocations.
claims.limitation: Cannot yet discriminate between carrier feed lag, inventory count drift, and dock capacity constraints; next diagnostic must isolate the specific downstream blocker

contradictions.description: C003 claims v18 split-reservation logic is the root cause; C005 claims the root cause is downstream (carrier/inventory/dock). Revert outcome (m8_r_revert) shows v18 is not the cause.
contradictions.discriminating_evidence_needed: Inventory count inspection and carrier feed status confirmation to isolate downstream blocker

resolutions.outcome: C003 disproven; C005 is the correct root cause
resolutions.rationale: m8_r_revert shows revert to v17 did not fix the held orders, meaning the allocation rule logic is not the cause. The issue persists under v17, indicating a downstream constraint.

next_action.rationale: Discriminating evidence: determine if east-node inventory count is exhausted or drifted, preventing fulfillment of any allocated orders. This rules out or confirms inventory_count_drift mechanism.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Inventory status will rule out or confirm inventory drift; if inventory is adequate, the blocker is carrier-side (feed lag or dock capacity)
